title: English Vocabulary in Use — Advanced (3rd Edition) · Units 47–48
description: Advanced vocabulary for print journalism, publishing formats, digital media, email communication and internet terminology, with usage and register distinctions.
sourceNotice: Prepared from the user-provided book for personal study. Vocabulary selection follows the teaching pages, exercises and answer key; translations, usage notes and example sentences are independently authored. Original textbook exercises, extended passages and illustrations have not been reproduced.

audit.scope: Complete teaching sections, numbered glossary notes, tables, exercises 47.1–47.5 and 48.1–48.4, and corresponding answer-key entries for Units 47 and 48.
audit.pronunciation: Conservative broad British IPA supplied for selected shorter entries. IPA is blank where reliable segmental pronunciation and stress were not confidently checked; longer expressions do not attempt connected-speech transcriptions.
audit.languagePolicy: All explanations, examples and metadata are in English; Brazilian Portuguese appears only in pt fields.
audit.reviewMethod: Compared the source study pages and exercises with the answer key; independently reviewed coverage, accurate meanings and register, British usage, unique IDs, original examples, provenance, item structure, and short TTS-target spellings. Static JSON and schema checks were run.
audit.limitations: No bundled MP3 files are provided. Live VocabLab import, browser TTS pronunciation and speech recognition have not been tested. Some digital terminology reflects the 2017 textbook, while notes clarify enduring or older usage.

units.title: Unit 47 — The media: in print
units.source: English Vocabulary in Use — Advanced (3rd Edition); printed pages 100–101 (PDF pages 102–103).
units.bookTitle: English Vocabulary in Use — Advanced (3rd Edition)
units.category: Media and publishing · print genres, newspapers, books and editorial language
learningObjectives: Distinguish newspaper sections, including editorials, features, classifieds and obituaries.
Use names of printed publications and identify their readership, purpose and register.
Contrast the academic and personal senses of journal, and book versus magazine terminology.
Understand exercise-only publishing expressions such as ghostwriter, facsimile and small print.

sectionsChecked: A: newspaper and magazine sections, including notes and definitions
B: printed material table, including both meanings of journal
Exercises 47.1–47.5 and Unit 47 answer key, including book and magazine terminology

items.pt: obituários; seção de falecimentos do jornal
items.example: The weekend edition includes obituaries of two influential scientists.
items.note: Plural noun for notices or accounts of people who have recently died; an individual notice is an obituary.

items.pt: editorial; artigo que expressa a posição de um jornal
items.example: The editorial criticised the proposed restrictions on public information.
items.note: An editorial expresses the publication’s opinion, unlike a straight news report; also called a leader in British newspaper usage.

items.pt: editorial (de jornal, especialmente no inglês britânico)
items.example: The paper published a leader urging ministers to reconsider the policy.
items.note: In this media sense, leader is a British English term for an editorial, not a person in charge.

items.example: Several regional outlets cover the news from rural communities.
items.note: Cover means report on or deal with a subject; the associated noun is coverage.

items.pt: cobertura jornalística; maneira como um assunto é noticiado
items.example: The election received extensive coverage in the national press.
items.note: Uncountable in the news-reporting sense; often extensive, balanced or biased coverage.

items.example: They advertised the second-hand piano in the local classified ads.
items.note: Short advertisements arranged by category; also called the classifieds.

items.pt: suplemento; caderno adicional de jornal ou revista
items.example: The science supplement contains interviews with several climate researchers.
items.note: A separate section or magazine accompanying a newspaper, not necessarily a dietary supplement.

items.pt: reportagem especial; artigo aprofundado sobre um tema
items.example: The monthly magazine ran a feature on advances in battery research.
items.note: A substantial piece about a particular topic, as distinct from a brief news item.

items.pt: coluna de aconselhamento sobre problemas pessoais
items.example: Readers send questions about relationships to the agony column.
items.note: Traditional British magazine or newspaper section answering personal or emotional questions.

items.pt: conselheira de coluna de assuntos pessoais
items.example: The agony aunt suggested that the reader discuss the problem openly.
items.note: Traditional, often gendered British term for an advice-column writer; not a literal family relationship.

items.pt: tiragem em circulação; número de exemplares distribuídos ou vendidos
items.example: The publication reported a rise in circulation after its redesign.
items.note: In publishing, the number of copies distributed or sold; not the same as readership.

items.example: The findings appeared in a peer-reviewed engineering journal.
items.note: In academic publishing, a periodical containing specialised research; different from a newspaper.

items.example: During the field trip, she kept a journal of her observations.
items.note: Can also mean a personal written record kept over time; do not confuse with an academic journal.

items.example: The research centre sends a monthly newsletter to its subscribers.
items.note: A periodic update intended for members or readers of a particular organisation or group.

items.pt: panfleto; folheto de discussão, frequentemente política
items.example: The charity distributed a pamphlet outlining its policy recommendations.
items.note: Usually a short, soft-covered publication, sometimes expressing a political position.

items.example: The university issued a press release about its new research partnership.
items.note: An official announcement prepared for the media; common collocation: issue a press release.

items.pt: folheto informativo, geralmente de uma ou poucas folhas
items.example: Visitors can pick up a leaflet describing the exhibition.
items.note: Typically one printed sheet, possibly folded, providing concise information.

items.pt: folheto ou catálogo ilustrado de divulgação
items.example: The travel agency sent us a brochure showing its winter tours.
items.note: Usually a small illustrated publication advertising a product, service or destination.

items.pt: prospecto; guia informativo de universidade, escola ou empresa
items.example: The postgraduate prospectus explains the entry requirements for each programme.
items.note: A publication describing an institution or opportunity; also used for investment offerings in finance.

items.example: Volunteers handed out flyers announcing the public lecture.
items.note: A single promotional sheet, commonly distributed to passers-by.

items.example: Each attendee received a booklet with the workshop schedule.
items.note: A thin, usually soft-covered small book; not necessarily advertising material.

items.example: The maintenance manual specifies the correct calibration procedure.
items.note: A reference containing instructions for operating or maintaining something.

items.example: The title is printed in gold on the spine of the book.
items.note: The bound edge of a book, often bearing the title and author.

items.pt: texto curto de apresentação na capa ou contracapa de livro
items.example: The blurb made the novel sound far more suspenseful than it was.
items.note: Promotional summary printed on or near a book cover; distinct from a review.

items.pt: prefácio de apresentação, muitas vezes escrito por outra pessoa
items.example: A leading historian wrote the foreword to the new edition.
items.note: Introductory text placed before the main work; often written by someone other than the author.

items.pt: índice remissivo de assuntos e nomes
items.example: Look up the topic in the index to find the relevant pages.
items.note: Alphabetical listing of subjects with page references; distinct from the contents page.

items.pt: assinatura de periódico; plano de recebimento
items.example: Her annual subscription includes twelve issues of the journal.
items.note: Payment or arrangement to receive a publication regularly; often an annual subscription.

items.pt: edição específica ou número de revista ou jornal
items.example: The April issue focuses on sustainable architecture.
items.note: One dated or numbered instalment of a periodical; distinguish from issue meaning problem.

items.pt: edição; versão publicada de livro, revista ou jornal
items.example: The revised edition includes a substantially expanded glossary.
items.note: A particular published version; unlike issue, it can be used of books as well as periodicals.

items.pt: trimestral; publicação lançada a cada três meses
items.example: The society produces a quarterly magazine about industrial heritage.
items.note: May describe something published every three months or refer to the periodical itself.

items.pt: escritor contratado que redige um texto assinado por outra pessoa
items.example: The athlete worked with a ghostwriter on her autobiography.
items.note: Writes material credited to someone else, generally with that person’s agreement; not necessarily unauthorised.

items.pt: editoração eletrônica; diagramação e produção de publicações no computador
items.example: Desktop publishing software enabled the club to design its own magazine.
items.note: Preparing printed or digital page layouts using a computer, rather than simply publishing on the internet.

items.pt: fac-símile; reprodução fiel de um documento ou edição
items.example: The archive produced a facsimile of the nineteenth-century manuscript.
items.note: An accurate reproduction of an original, preserving its appearance; not simply a modernised version.

items.pt: requisitos de ingresso; critérios de admissão
items.example: The university lists entry requirements for applicants from different countries.
items.note: Qualifications or conditions that an applicant must meet before joining an institution or course.

items.pt: revelar problemas graves; denunciar falhas sérias
items.example: The investigation exposed serious problems in the distribution system.
items.note: Expose here means uncover and make known facts that were not previously public.

items.example: The leaflet draws attention to the risks of inadequate ventilation.
items.note: Fixed construction: draw attention to something, not draw attention on something.

items.example: The short guide is packed with useful tips for new researchers.
items.note: Packed with emphasises a high concentration of content; often promotional and positive.

items.pt: letras miúdas; cláusulas e condições pouco visíveis
items.example: Read the small print before accepting the extended warranty.
items.note: Fine details or restrictions in agreements or promotional offers; usually uncountable.

items.word: tell you all you need to know
items.pt: dar todas as informações essenciais sobre algo
items.example: The handbook tells you all you need to know about registration.
items.note: Informal promotional expression meaning to provide all the essential information.

units.title: Unit 48 — The media: internet and email
units.source: English Vocabulary in Use — Advanced (3rd Edition); printed pages 102–103 (PDF pages 104–105).
units.bookTitle: English Vocabulary in Use — Advanced (3rd Edition)
units.category: Digital media · internet technologies, communication and online language
learningObjectives: Use digital communication and web-service vocabulary naturally, including email and online communities.
Distinguish upload/download, inbox/outbox, online/offline and install/uninstall in context.
Explain internet risks, privacy terminology and common communication errors.
Understand prefixed e- expressions and exercise-only terms with appropriate pronunciation.

sectionsChecked: A: pros and cons of internet use, numbered vocabulary notes and categories
B: email and internet communications, including phrasal verbs
Exercises 48.1–48.4 and Unit 48 answer key, including opposite pairs and e- forms

items.pt: prós e contras; vantagens e desvantagens
items.example: The committee discussed the pros and cons of remote teaching.
items.note: A fixed expression weighing advantages against disadvantages; typically plural.

items.example: The group uses instant messaging for urgent project updates.
items.note: Near-real-time text communication between users, unlike conventional delayed correspondence.

items.example: The community opened a chat room for participants to exchange ideas.
items.note: An online space where several users can hold a text-based discussion.

items.pt: grupo de discussão on-line, especialmente dos sistemas tradicionais da internet
items.example: A specialist newsgroup helped researchers exchange troubleshooting advice.
items.note: A forum for shared interests, historically associated with Usenet; less common in everyday usage today.

items.example: The museum shares short videos on a social networking site.
items.note: A platform for connecting users and sharing personal or professional content.

items.example: The association hosted a webinar about publishing research responsibly.
items.note: An online seminar, often involving a speaker and an audience that can ask questions.

items.example: The retailer expanded into e-commerce without opening new shops.
items.note: Commercial transactions conducted through electronic networks, especially the internet.

items.example: Internet banking allows customers to review transactions without visiting a branch.
items.note: Managing a bank account online; often called online banking.

items.example: I prefer an e-book when travelling because it weighs nothing in my bag.
items.note: Electronic book read on a device; distinct from a physical printed copy.

items.example: The training provider introduced e-learning modules for new staff.
items.note: Learning activities delivered through digital systems, commonly over the internet.

items.example: She browsed several academic websites before choosing a course.
items.note: Often suggests looking through pages without a narrowly specified goal.

items.pt: navegar pela internet, passando de uma página para outra
items.example: He spent the evening surfing the web for examples of accessible design.
items.note: Informal expression for moving around websites; overlaps with browse the web.

items.example: The presentation includes a graphic image showing the network topology.
items.note: Images may include diagrams, icons and illustrations, not only photographs.

items.example: The tutor attached a sound file demonstrating the pronunciation.
items.note: A digital file containing audio data; often used for recordings and speech.

items.example: Please include the signed form as an attachment to your email.
items.note: A file sent together with an email; typically attach a file or send an attachment.

items.example: The institution introduced a secure file-sharing platform for project documents.
items.note: Sharing data or files over a network; spelling also appears without a hyphen.

items.example: Online gaming lets participants cooperate with people in other countries.
items.note: Playing games over a network, often with remote players.

items.example: The internet service provider reported a temporary outage.
items.note: A company supplying internet connectivity and, sometimes, additional online services.

items.pt: provedor de acesso à internet (sigla em inglês)
items.example: We contacted our ISP after the connection repeatedly failed.
items.note: Initialism for Internet Service Provider; pronounce the letters individually, not as a word.

items.example: Someone tried to hack an account by guessing an old password.
items.note: Here hack means gain unauthorised access, not legitimate programming or security research.

items.pt: baixar; transferir um arquivo da internet para o dispositivo
items.example: Download the installer from the official project website.
items.note: Move data from a remote system to your own device; contrasted with upload.

items.pt: enviar; transferir um arquivo do dispositivo para um serviço on-line
items.example: You must upload the completed application before midnight.
items.note: Move data from your device to a remote system; contrasted with download.

items.example: The mail filter placed the unwanted advertisements in the spam folder.
items.note: Unsolicited bulk messages, frequently advertising; usually uncountable.

items.example: The account automatically moves suspicious offers to junk mail.
items.note: In digital communication, an informal synonym for unwanted promotional messages.

items.example: The app was designed to be entertaining but became surprisingly addictive.
items.note: Adjective describing an activity that is difficult to stop doing; avoid treating ordinary enjoyment as dependence.

items.pt: cookie; dado que um site armazena no navegador
items.example: The website asks users to accept cookies before saving preferences.
items.note: Browser-stored data used for sessions, preferences or tracking; not itself necessarily executable software.

items.example: The platform provides a way to report offensive material.
items.note: Content likely to cause serious offence, including some abusive or hateful material.

items.pt: controles parentais; recursos de restrição para crianças
items.example: Parents can enable parental controls on shared devices.
items.note: Settings that restrict access to websites, content or activities; commonly plural.

items.example: Bookmark the article so you can return to it during your research.
items.note: Verb meaning save a website address for later access; the saved link is a bookmark.

items.example: The organisation updated its home page with the latest announcement.
items.note: The main entry page of a website; also written homepage.

items.pt: inscrever-se em um grupo de discussão
items.example: Several specialists subscribed to the newsgroup to follow technical debates.
items.note: Use subscribe to, not subscribe in; this meaning is membership or regular access to updates.

items.pt: filtrar; impedir que algo indesejado passe
items.example: The security tool screens out messages from known malicious senders.
items.note: Separable phrasal verb: screen out unwanted messages or screen them out.

items.example: The system filters out obvious spam before delivery.
items.note: Separable phrasal verb: remove undesirable items from a stream or collection.

items.example: The mail server was unavailable during scheduled maintenance.
items.note: A computer or service that supplies resources to other computers or users.

items.pt: estar fora do ar; não estar funcionando (sistema)
items.example: The website was down for twenty minutes after the update.
items.note: Informal use of down for a computer, website or service that is not operating.

items.example: The team updated its anti-virus software before connecting the test laptop.
items.note: Software intended to detect or block malicious programs; often written antivirus.

items.example: Update the software regularly to correct security vulnerabilities.
items.note: An update can provide fixes and new features; the opposite downdate is not standard English.

items.pt: voltar ao remetente por falha de entrega (mensagem)
items.example: My email bounced because the recipient’s address no longer existed.
items.note: With email, bounce means fail to be delivered and return to the sender.

items.example: The team posts its monthly progress reports online.
items.note: Post is a verb meaning publish content on a website or social platform.

items.example: Delete the temporary files after the transfer has been verified.
items.note: Remove data from a device or application; compare undelete for reversing deletion.

items.example: The recovery tool can undelete a document from the recycle bin.
items.note: A computing verb meaning reverse a deletion where recovery is possible.

items.example: The message remained unread in her inbox until Monday.
items.note: Location for received email; paired with outbox for outgoing messages.

items.example: The email stayed in the outbox while the connection was unavailable.
items.note: Folder containing outgoing messages awaiting transmission; not equivalent to Sent Items.

items.example: The documentation is available online to registered users.
items.note: Connected to or accessible through a network; opposite offline.

items.example: You can edit the document offline and synchronise it later.
items.note: Not currently connected to the internet; opposite online.

items.example: Install the approved driver before connecting the interface.
items.note: Put software in place so that it can be used; opposite uninstall.

items.example: Uninstall the older application before deploying its replacement.
items.note: Remove installed software; unlike delete, typically removes an application through a removal process.

items.example: The contract was approved using an e-signature.
items.note: Electronic method indicating consent or signing; specific legal requirements vary by jurisdiction.

items.pt: habilitado para uso eletrônico; disponibilizado digitalmente
items.example: The course was e-enabled so students could access its materials remotely.
items.note: Describes something adapted to be available or usable through electronic systems.

items.pt: economia das empresas que operam pela internet
items.example: Many start-ups emerged during the rapid expansion of the dotcom economy.
items.note: Refers to internet-based commercial activity, especially businesses associated with .com addresses.

items.pt: tablet; computador portátil com tela sensível ao toque
items.example: She uses a tablet to review research articles while travelling.
items.note: A portable touchscreen computing device; distinct from a conventional laptop.
